item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "Implement `retry_budget.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: implement retry_budget.py exactly to SPEC.md in the repository root.
Acceptance criteria:
- Every documented API name, signature and return/raise behaviour in SPEC.md is preserved.
- Every error case and boundary case in SPEC.md is handled explicitly; failures are not swallowed.
- Add focused tests covering each error and boundary case, in addition to the existing basic tests. Existing tests must still pass.
- Standard library only; no new dependencies.
- Run the test suite and report the result.
- Commit the work to the local branch with a clear message. Do not push. Do not add attribution lines naming any AI tool.

Constraints: follow the repository's existing style; keep functions short, validate inputs at the boundary, and avoid silent fallbacks.

reasons: sizer: ordinary -> medium; unchanged: the learned route's effort

pr.body: Files: retry_budget.py (validation helpers, saturating backoff, retry_delay), test_retry_budget.py (19 new tests for each error and boundary case in SPEC.md). Approach: all args validated as built-in int before any early return; backoff min(cap, base<<(attempt-1)) with shortcut when the shift exceeds cap.bit_length(), so huge attempts never build large powers; Retry-After applied as uncapped minimum; None when elapsed+delay >= budget. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v -> before 3 errors (NotImplementedError), after Ran 22 tests OK. Review: one reviewer, pass on 3a0a833, no blocking findings; two non-blocking coverage follow-ups (float budget_ms/cap_ms and bool/float max_attempts tests; no test pins shift == cap.bit_length() with small cap). Assumptions: no repository contributor guidance file found; standard library only.

risk.why: Pure function in one module plus tests; no behaviour outside the new function, no I/O, concurrency or persistence. Review pass at low risk.
